findings.finding: Camissa Asset Management (South Africa) is selling down steadily into the print: 14.51% before 28 Aug -> 13.58% (28 Aug) -> 12.93% (22 Sep) -> 11.95% (c.1-2 Oct) -> 10.93% (12 Oct), i.e. about 2.4m shares between the last two notices against roughly 0.4m shares a day of median turnover, with 25.2m shares still held, so a large, active seller will be there to supply into any results-day strength.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior results day observed with a disclosed seller this active; the stock rose 12% on 17 Sep while Camissa was already selling, so the seller has not stopped a positive surprise from landing.

findings.finding: The upgraded FY27 guide builds in a sharp H2 slowdown: with H1 GP c.+18% and FY GP low-to-mid teens, H2 GP growth is roughly high single digits, and with H1 OP c.+6% and FY OP low-to-mid single digits, H2 OP is roughly flat to low single digits. findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced, and inside guidance: it was published five weeks before Bytes raised its guide, so the company guided with it known. It survives only as an H2 commentary risk if management quantifies it. This is a distributor's proxy, not a Bytes statement.
